claims.text: Adding approximately 1–2 at.% reactive elements to CoCrFeNi-based alloys improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Adding approximately 1–2 at.% reactive elements improves the material integrity of CoCrFeNi-based alloys during high-temperature oxidation.
Reactive dopants segregate to grain boundaries in the forming oxide scale.
Dopant segregation reduces the interfacial energy of oxide-scale grain boundaries.
Dopant segregation limits oxygen diffusion through the oxide scale.
The initial CoCrFeNi-based alloy has a uniform elemental distribution under standard processing conditions.
Yttrium and hafnium are suitable examples of reactive dopants for the proposed modification.
High-temperature exposure drives the proposed dopants to oxide-scale grain boundaries.
Reduced oxide grain-boundary energy inhibits rapid oxygen diffusion.
Dopant segregation promotes formation of a finer protective oxide layer.
Dopant segregation promotes formation of a more adherent protective oxide layer.
Dopant segregation promotes formation of a defect-free protective oxide layer.
The oxide scale on doped alloys grows more slowly than that on undoped alloys.
Undoped CoCrFeNi-based alloys form a less optimal oxide scale than the proposed doped alloys.
The less optimal scale on undoped alloys causes faster oxidation kinetics.
The less optimal scale on undoped alloys reduces structural integrity under the test conditions.
The proposed beneficial effect holds from 980–1050°C for oxidation exposures up to 100 hours.
Interactions between the reactive dopants and base-alloy components may alter segregation kinetics and oxide-scale evolution.
